                                             PROJECT NO. 58481

     RULEMAKING TO IMPLEMENT                                §          PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION
     LARGE LOAD INTERCONNECTION                             §
     STANDARDS UNDER PURA § 37.0561                         §                          OF TEXAS

                                POST-WORKSHOP COMMENTS OF
                              TEXAS ELECTRIC COOPERATIVES, INC.

         Texas Electric Cooperatives, Inc. (TEC) respectfully submits these comments in response

to the discussion at the Commission Staff (Staff) led workshop regarding PUC Project No. 58481

on January 9, 2025. 1 TEC is the statewide association of electric cooperatives operating in Texas,

representing its members except as their interests may be separately represented. 2 Commission

Staff requested written feedback by Friday, January 16. These comments are timely filed.

                                                   I.       Comments

1.       Definition of “Interconnecting Utility”

         TEC appreciates the efforts of Commission Staff to work with stakeholders to ensure that

 the proposed rule effectively works for all types of utilities. It was apparent from the discussion at

 the workshop that there needs to be some further delineation between the interconnecting retail

 provider and the interconnecting transmission service provider (“TSP”).

         An example multi-party scenario which needs to be addressed in the rule is a situation

 addressed in PURA §37.056(f) where a transmission-owning electric cooperative will be building

the transmission facilities to serve a member’s load and those transmission facilities will

interconnect with another TSP that owns existing transmission. In this situation, the TSP studying

the large load interconnection will be the TSP that owns the existing transmission facilities, but


1
 Staff Memo and January 9 Workshop Agenda w/Attachments (Jan. 2, 2026).
2
  TEC’s 76 members include distribution cooperatives that provide retail electric utility service to approximately
5,000,000 consumers in statutorily authorized service areas that encompass more than half of the total area of the state.
TEC’s G&T members generally acquire generation resources and power supply for their member distribution
cooperatives and deliver electricity to them at wholesale.


                                                                                                                       1
 the studying TSP will not be the owner the new transmission facilities which will actually

interconnect to the large load customer. Both TSPs in this situation will have costs to be recovered

related to the interconnection of the large load.

       There are likely several other multi-party scenarios which could exist; therefore, the rule

needs to have more flexibility in the definition of “interconnecting utility.”

       One potential solution would be to amend the definition of “interconnecting utility” and

add a definition for “interconnecting transmission service provider” as follows:

       Interconnecting utility (ies) includes one or more of the following, as
       applicable–

           A. an electric utility, municipally owned utility, or electric cooperative

               that is certificated to serve the interconnecting large load customer

               at retail or, if the certificated utility designates, the interconnecting

               transmission service provider and/or

           B. for purposes of interconnection studies, facilities planning,

               interconnection and ERCOT coordination, the Interconnecting

               Transmission Service Provider.

       Interconnecting Transmission Service Provider: An electric utility,

       municipally owned utility, or electric cooperative that owns and operates

       existing facilities necessary to interconnect a large load customer to the

       ERCOT transmission network and/or future facilities to which the large load

       customer will connect.


       In the alternative, if the proposed definition is unworkable with all stakeholders, TEC

recommends removing the term “interconnecting utility” altogether and replacing it with two

separate terms: the “interconnecting retail service provider” which can have the same definition as

“interconnecting utility” in the current draft but without the ability to designate the transmission



                                                                                                  2
 service provider, and the “interconnecting transmission service provider”, defined as “a

transmission service provider that owns and operates the existing facilities necessary to

interconnect a large load customer to the ERCOT transmission network.”

           Additionally, regardless of the definitions used, the duties currently assigned to the

“interconnecting utility” in the discussion draft will need to be clearly divided among the retail

and transmission utilities, in case they are separate entities. For example, the interconnecting TSP

performing studies should be the TSP with the existing facilities.

2.          Jurisdictional Issues

           TEC reiterates it verbal comments from the workshop and written comments submitted on

the previous discussion draft. 3 Items such as CIAC involve the passing of costs to large loads and

elements of ratemaking and interconnection processes that are still reserved to the electric

cooperative. 4 TEC does not dispute that Senate Bill 6 applies to electric cooperatives, but Senate

Bill 6, because it intersects areas of cooperative jurisdiction, must be strictly construed so that

anything beyond the plain language of statute, such as timelines and the passing of costs, is not

applicable to an electric cooperative.

                                                 II.      Conclusion

           TEC appreciates the opportunity to provide comment following the workshop and looks

forward to working with the Commission and other stakeholders on this project.




3
    Comments of Texas Electric Cooperatives, Inc. at 7 – 8 (Dec. 19, 2025).
4
    See Public Utility Regulatory Act (PURA) § 35.004 (c-2); See also PURA § 41.055 (1).
